RESEARCH ONLY. Do not write any files or code. Return findings as your final message text. Use WebFetch/WebSearch and curl via Bash. Cite a URL for every factual claim. QUOTE exact clauses verbatim where asked.

Topic: Steam Workshop as a mod source for a game-server HOSTING company (they want to index workshop items in a catalog and one-click install them onto customer game servers: Garry's Mod, ARK SE/ASA, Project Zomboid, Rust maps, Space Engineers, Barotrauma, CS2, Killing Floor 2, Unturned, Don't Starve Together, Conan Exiles).

Cover ALL of these:

A) Steam Web API endpoints for workshop metadata:
1. POST https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/ — actually TEST it live with curl (it needs no API key; POST form fields itemcount=1&publishedfileids[0]=<id>). Use a real Garry's Mod or ARK workshop id. Report the EXACT full field list returned (title, description, preview_url, file_url, hcontent_file, filename, file_size, time_created, time_updated, consumer_app_id, creator_app_id, creator, subscriptions, favorited, views, tags, banned, result, lifetime_subscriptions, etc.). Note which apps return a direct file_url (legacy single-file items) vs. 0/empty (UGC items needing steamcmd).
2. IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1 — requires a Web API key. Document the query params (query_type, cursor, numperpage, appid, requiredtags, return_metadata, return_details, return_tags, return_previews, return_children, return_vote_data, return_short_description, match_all_tags, search_text). Also IPublishedFileService/GetDetails/v1. Cite the docs (steamapi.xpaw.me, partner.steamgames.com, steamwebapi docs).
3. ISteamRemoteStorage/GetCollectionDetails/v1 for collections.
4. How do you get a Steam Web API key and what are its terms (steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey)?

B) steamcmd +workshop_download_item <appid> <pubfileid>:
- Does anonymous login (+login anonymous) work? For WHICH appids? Find concrete evidence (developer.valvesoftware.com wiki, SteamCMD docs, forum/reddit/GitHub issue threads, hosting-panel docs like Pterodactyl eggs, LinuxGSM source). LinuxGSM and Pterodactyl egg scripts are excellent evidence — look at how they actually do it.
- What is the known limitation about needing an account that OWNS the game? Quote/cite.
- Known workarounds hosting companies use (a dedicated purchased steam account, the "app_update <appid> then workshop_download_item" pattern, steamworkshopdownloader.io style services). Report factually, don't endorse.
- Where do downloaded files land on disk (steamapps/workshop/content/<appid>/<pubfileid>)?

C) LEGAL — quote exact clauses with URLs:
- Steam Subscriber Agreement https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ — find and QUOTE the clauses about Content and Services, licensing, and any restriction on distributing/copying.
- Steam Web API Terms of Use https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms — QUOTE it in full or near-full (it is short). Note restrictions on caching, commercial use, and redistribution.
- Steam Workshop Legal Agreement https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/workshoplegalagreement — QUOTE the license the uploader grants Valve and whether it extends to third parties/sublicensing.
- Steam Online Conduct / Steam Distribution Agreement if relevant.
- Is a hosting company permitted to download and install workshop items onto customer servers? Report what the documents actually say and where they are silent/ambiguous. Be explicit about ambiguity — do NOT guess.
- Find any real evidence of what hosting companies actually do today: Nitrado, G-Portal, Apex Hosting, Shockbyte, PingPerfect, Host Havoc — their documented workshop-install features (help/KB articles), and any public statement from Valve or those companies about permission. Also Pterodactyl/Pelican egg install scripts that call steamcmd for workshop items.

Be thorough. Be explicit about what you could and could not verify.

## Key Components

Server-side Workshop content involves three pieces: a Workshop collection (a list of addons on Steam that your server should load), a Steam Web API key (lets your server query the Workshop and download the collection), and resource.AddWorkshop (a small Lua script that tells joining players which addons to download).

- Treat your API key like a password, since anyone with it can act on the Workshop through your Steam account's API access. Never share it publicly or commit it to public files.
- On boot, the console will show it downloading and mounting each addon in the collection. The first start after adding a large collection can take several minutes.

content.text:
Research complete. Findings below. Everything marked **TESTED LIVE** was executed with curl from this box today (2026-09-19).

---

# A) Steam Web API — workshop metadata

## A1. `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/` — TESTED LIVE ✅

**No API key required.** Confirmed working, POST form-encoded. It is absent from `partner.steamgames.com` docs but **is** in Valve's own machine-readable interface list:

```
curl -s 'https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamWebAPIUtil/GetSupportedAPIList/v1/'
→ ISteamRemoteStorage / GetPublishedFileDetails v1 POST
    - itemcount        uint32 REQUIRED  "Number of items being requested"
    - publishedfileids[0] uint64 REQUIRED "published file id to look up"
```
(Source: `https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamWebAPIUtil/GetSupportedAPIList/v1/`, fetched live.)

### Exact full field list returned

Live call for GMod item `104606562`:

```
publishedfileid   "104606562"        string
result            1                  int   (EResult; 1 = OK)
creator           "76561197996891752" string (SteamID64 of uploader)
creator_app_id    4000               int
consumer_app_id   4000               int
filename          ""                 string
file_size         "4934"             string (bytes, as string)
file_url          ""                 string
hcontent_file     "3191657044292712912" string
preview_url       "https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/572275840012030224/E631…/"
hcontent_preview  "572275840012030224" string
title             "Achievement Viewer"
description       "…"                (raw Steam BBCode, NOT html)
time_created      1351181451         int (unix)
time_updated      1701637018         int (unix)
visibility        0                  int (0 = public)
banned            0                  int
ban_reason        ""                 string
subscriptions     128564             int  (current)
favorited         4760               int  (current)
lifetime_subscriptions 419311        int
lifetime_favorited     5878          int
views             79909              int
tags              [{"tag":"Addon"},{"tag":"tool"},{"tag":"Fun"}]
```

Fields **not** present that you may be expecting: no `vote_data`/score, no `short_description`, no `children` (collections), no `app_name`, no `language`, no `revision`. Those only come from `IPublishedFileService/*` (key required).

Missing/deleted items return a stub: `{"publishedfileid":"1234567890","result":9}` — EResult 9 = `k_EResultFileNotFound`. **TESTED LIVE.** Your indexer must handle `result != 1` per item, not per response (`response.result` is still 1).

### `file_url`: legacy vs. UGC — this is the key finding

**TESTED LIVE across all your target games.** `file_url` is empty for every modern item. It is populated only for legacy single-file cloud items and for screenshots:

| App | appid | Item tested | `file_url` | `filename` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Garry's Mod | 4000 | 104606562, 3801628931 | **empty** | empty |
| ARK: SE | 346110 | 731604991 (S+), 3800330076 | **empty** | empty |
| Project Zomboid | 108600 | 2478768005 | **empty** | empty |
| Rust | 252490 | 3613230294 | **empty** | empty |
| Space Engineers | 244850 | 3791989881 | **empty** | empty |
| Barotrauma | 602960 | 3800111304 | **empty** | empty |
| Killing Floor 2 | 232090 | 3768281610 | **empty** | empty (`file_size` "0") |
| Conan Exiles | 440900 | 3384531957 | **empty** | empty |
| Unturned | 304930 | 3799215306 | **empty** | empty |
| **Don't Starve Together** | **322330** | **375850593** | **POPULATED** | `mod_publish_data_file.zip` |
| CS2 screenshot | 730 | 1928543775 | **POPULATED** | `730/screenshots/2019…jpg` |

**DST is the outlier and it is fully exploitable.** I downloaded it with a plain unauthenticated GET — no Steam account, no steamcmd, no API key:

```
curl "https://cdn.steamusercontent.com/ugc/273967538676883524/4F07DDD67C49CB3F746E78B36016D2A00739BEF8/"
→ HTTP=200 bytes=32910 content-type=application/octet-stream
→ file: Zip archive data
```
32910 bytes exactly matches the reported `file_size`. DST uses the old ISteamRemoteStorage publishing path, so its workshop content is a public CDN object. Treat this as a legal question, not a technical one (see §C).

**`hcontent_file` cannot be turned into a URL.** TESTED — all three CDN host patterns 404 for ARK S+'s `hcontent_file`:
```
https://steamusercontent-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2062549808985904415/  → 404
https://cdn.steamusercontent.com/ugc/2062549808985904415/          → 404
https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/2062549808985904415/       → 404
```
For UGC items, `hcontent_file` is a SteamPipe manifest handle, only resolvable through the Steam content system (i.e. steamcmd or `ISteamUGC::DownloadItem`). **There is no HTTP shortcut.**

### Operational limits — TESTED LIVE
- **Batching works to at least 100 items per call** (10/50/100 all returned `resultcount` matching, all 200 OK). I did not probe above 100.
- 10 rapid sequential keyless calls: all `200`. No rate-limit headers observed.
- Only cache header returned is `expires:` (~30 min out). No `Cache-Control`, no `ETag`.
- `preview_url` is a public CDN image URL and is hotlinkable — but see §C on the API ToU.

## A2. `IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1` — key REQUIRED

**TESTED LIVE, keyless:**
```
GET .../IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1/?query_type=9&appid=4000&cursor=*
→ HTTP 403  "Access is denied. Retrying will not help. Please verify your key= parameter."
```
`IPublishedFileService/GetDetails/v1/` keyless → **HTTP 401**. Both need a user-level Web API key.

Full parameter list, from `https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/IPublishedFileService`:

| Param | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Steamworks Web API user authentication key |
| `query_type` | uint32 | EPublishedFileQueryType enum |
| `page` | uint32 | max 1000 |
| `cursor` | string | pagination; **use `*` initially** — use this, not `page`, for deep indexing |
| `numperpage` | uint32 | results per page |
| `creator_appid` | uint32 | app that *created* the files |
| `appid` | uint32 | app that *consumes* the files |
| `requiredtags` | string | tags to match |
| `excludedtags` | string | tags that must NOT be present |
| `match_all_tags` | bool | require all vs. at least one |
| `required_flags` / `omitted_flags` | string | |
| `search_text` | string | matches title/description |
| `filetype` | uint32 | EPublishedFileInfoMatchingFileType |
| `child_publishedfileid` | uint64 | find items referencing this item |
| `days` | uint32 | for trend queries, [1,7] |
| `include_recent_votes_only` | bool | |
| `cache_max_age_seconds` | uint32 | allow stale data |
| `language` | int32 | defaults to English |
| `required_kv_tags` | message | key-value tags |
| `totalonly` | bool | return count only |
| `ids_only` | bool | return ids only |
| `return_vote_data` | bool | |
| `return_tags` | bool | |
| `return_kv_tags` | bool | |
| `return_previews` | bool | preview images/videos |
| `return_children` | bool | child item ids |
| `return_short_description` | bool | short vs. full description |
| `return_for_sale_data` | bool | pricing |
| `return_metadata` | bool | populate metadata field |
| `return_playtime_stats` | uint32 | playtime stats for N days |

The other `IPublishedFileService` methods (`Delete`, `SetDeveloperMetadata`, `UpdateAppUGCBan`, `UpdateBanStatus`, `UpdateIncompatibleStatus`, `UpdateTags`) require a **publisher** key — not available to you; you are not the app's publisher.

**Practical consequence for a catalog:** `QueryFiles` is the only discovery/search endpoint, it requires a key, and that key is bound by the 100k/day cap and the "personal to you" clause in §C.

## A3. `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetCollectionDetails/v1/` — TESTED LIVE ✅

**No key required.** POST `collectioncount=1&publishedfileids[0]=<id>`. Live result for collection `180077636`:
```json
{"response":{"result":1,"resultcount":1,"collectiondetails":[{
  "publishedfileid":"180077636","result":1,
  "children":[{"publishedfileid":"175394472","sortorder":0,"filetype":0}, …]}]}}
```
Returns only ids + sort order + filetype — **no titles**. You must fan out to `GetPublishedFileDetails` (which batches 100+) to hydrate. Two-call pattern per collection.

## A4. Getting a Steam Web API key

`https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey` — requires a logged-in Steam account (returns an empty body to unauthenticated curl; I could not fetch the signup form itself). Per Valve's own docs at `https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi_overview/auth`: *"The standard user keys are available to everyone, all that is required is a Steam account and the domain name"* — no game-ownership requirement, but you register a domain and accept the API ToU. Terms quoted in full in §C2.

---

# B) `steamcmd +workshop_download_item`

## B1. Does `+login anonymous` work? It is a **per-app developer opt-in**

This is the single most important operational fact, and it is not what most people assume.

Anonymous workshop download is controlled by a checkbox the *game's developer* sets in Steamworks. Two independent corroborating sources:

1. **Barotrauma bug report** — `https://github.com/FakeFishGames/Barotrauma/issues/7707`, titled *"Unable to use workshop_download_item with anonymous login in steamcmd"*. Exact failing command: `steamcmd +login anonymous +workshop_download_item 602960 2005463692 +quit`. Reporter: *"When using steamcmd's workshop_download_item command mod fails when not logged into an authenticated steam account."* The fix requested is for the **developer** to flip the Steamworks setting. **Still open.** → Barotrauma (602960) does **not** support anonymous workshop download.

2. **A developer actually flipping the switch, publicly** — GearCity dev thread, `https://steamcommunity.com/app/285110/discussions/0/686363730790031270/`. Dev Eric.B: *"Last I looked… there was no way to allow anonymous workshop downloads."* A user gave him the steps: *"Log in to your Steamworks partner site… Navigate to the page for your app… Scroll down to 'Technical tools'. Go to the 'Edit steamworks' setting. Click on the 'Workshop' tab. Find the setting titled 'Enable anonymous game servers to download workshop items' and check the corresponding checkbox."* Dev's follow-up: *"Found a few new features there. Done. Enjoy."* — and anonymous downloads then worked.

Valve's own partner docs acknowledge the anonymous-server case exists, at `https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/workshop/implementation`: *"Game servers can also download and install items"* and *"If the user is not subscribed to the item (e.g. a Game Server using anonymous login), the workshop item will be downloaded and cached temporarily."* But the docs give no per-app list and never name the checkbox.

**I could not verify anonymous support empirically per-appid** — doing so requires installing and running steamcmd, which is out of scope for a research-only task. **You must probe each of your 11 appids yourself** in a sandbox; there is no published list, and the setting is invisible from outside. Budget for this — it determines your whole architecture per game.

Note also the separate, related mechanism for the *server binaries* (not mods), from `https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/uploading/distributing_gs`: *"The dedicated server appID and associated depot(s) will be added to the anonymous steamcmd package (pkg 17906) to be downloadable using SteamCMD in anonymous mode."* That's why `+login anonymous +app_update <server_appid>` works everywhere while workshop download often doesn't. Two different gates.

## B2. The ownership limitation — quoted

The clearest statement I found is in a production hosting egg used by thousands of servers. Pterodactyl Arma 3 egg (`https://github.com/parkervcp/eggs/blob/master/game_eggs/steamcmd_servers/arma_arma3/egg-arma3.json`), variable descriptions verbatim:

> `STEAM_USER`: *"Used for installation and updates. **Account does not need to own Arma 3, but MUST BE a VALID Steam account (anonymous login cannot be used).** For security reasons it is recommended that you create a new Steam account just for your dedicated servers."*

> `DISABLE_MOD_UPDATES`: *"**If the Steam account does not own the base Arma 3 game, Steam Workshop mod downloads/updates will not work.** If so, this setting allows disabling of this feature to avoid errors. (1 Disable | 0 Enable)"*

Note the asymmetry it documents: server *binaries* need only a valid account; workshop *mods* need an account that **owns the game**.

Second corroboration, Space Engineers, via GTXGaming's KB (`https://www.gtxgaming.co.uk/clientarea/knowledgebase/568/How-to-add-mods-to-your-PC-Space-Engineers-server.html`): *"This requires a user and password of a Steam account which owns the Space Engineers game to get mods."*

Third: `https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/8028` — *"Unable to download workshop mod without owning game on account"*. Reporter: *"Either I am secure and I have to provide the password every time I wish to update my mods, thus getting rid of automation. Or I go against the recommendation and provide my main account's password in a script file for convenience."* **Open, no Valve response.** Valve has not addressed this publicly.

I found **no Valve-authored document** that states the ownership rule. It is documented only by the community and by hosts. Flag that as ambiguity, not settled fact.

## B3. Workarounds hosts/tooling actually use — reported, not endorsed

1. **Dedicated purchased Steam account with credentials in the panel.** Pterodactyl's standard steamcmd egg boilerplate takes `STEAM_USER`/`STEAM_PASS`/`STEAM_AUTH` and falls back to anonymous when blank:
   ```
   if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
       STEAM_USER=anonymous
   ```
   The Arma egg's own warning: *"This info is not visible to the server owner, BUT IS stored in PLAIN TEXT."* and *"Steam Guard MUST be completely TURNED OFF for install to complete successfully."* Disabling Steam Guard on a game-owning account whose password sits in plaintext in a panel database is the actual cost of this approach.

2. **The `+app_update` then `+workshop_download_item` pattern.** The Squad egg (`game_eggs/steamcmd_servers/squad/egg-squad.json`) is the only egg in the entire parkervcp catalogue (216 eggs) that calls `workshop_download_item`:
   ```bash
   rm /mnt/server/container/steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_393380.acf
   ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} \
     $(IFS=','; for item in $WORKSHOP_ITEMS; do echo "+workshop_download_item 393380 ${item}"; done) \
   mv -rf /mnt/server/container/steamapps/workshop/content/393380 /mnt/server/SquadGame/Plugins/Mods
   ```
   Note it downloads against the **game** appid 393380, not the server appid, and deletes the `.acf` state file to force re-download.

3. **Third-party downloader services** (`steamworkshopdownloader.io` — **live, HTTP 200, Cloudflare-fronted, as of today**). These proxy the download through their own Steam accounts. I found **no evidence of Valve enforcement action against them**, and equally no evidence of Valve permission. Reporting only; I would not build a commercial product on one.

4. **Sidestep steamcmd entirely — let the game server fetch it.** This is what the industry actually does (see B5/§C5).

## B4. Where files land on disk

`steamapps/workshop/content/<appid>/<publishedfileid>/` — confirmed by the Squad egg's own `mv` path (`/mnt/server/container/steamapps/workshop/content/393380`) and by Conan KB articles citing `steamapps/workshop/content/440900`. State/metadata lives alongside at `steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_<appid>.acf` (the Squad egg deletes exactly that file). With `+force_install_dir X`, the tree is `X/steamapps/workshop/content/<appid>/<pubfileid>/`.

## B5. Per-game reality check — **this materially changes your product scope**

I checked the actual mod-delivery mechanism for each of your 11 games. **Most of them do not need you to download anything at all** — you write an ID into a config file and the dedicated server pulls it through Steam itself.

| Game | Mechanism | Do *you* download files? |
|---|---|---|
| Garry's Mod | `+host_workshop_collection <id>` **+ `-authkey <Steam Web API key>`** | **No** — server downloads & mounts |
| ARK: SE (346110) | `ActiveMods=` / `-mods=` ModIDs | No — server auto-downloads |
| **ARK: ASA (2399830)** | **CurseForge, NOT Steam Workshop** | N/A — wrong platform entirely |
| Project Zomboid | `WorkshopItems=` + `Mods=` in `servertest.ini` | No |
| **Rust** | `server.levelurl "<direct .map URL>"` | **Workshop is skins-only, not maps** |
| Space Engineers | `<Mods>` in `sandbox_config.sbc` | Server downloads, but needs an owning account |
| Barotrauma | anonymous **fails**; manual upload or owning account | **Yes** |
| CS2 | `host_workshop_map` / `ds_workshop_changelevel` | No |
| Killing Floor 2 | `ServerSubscribedWorkshopItems` | No |
| Unturned | `Workshop_Download_IDs` in Commands.dat | No |
| Don't Starve Together | `dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua` | No (and legacy `file_url` is public anyway) |
| Conan Exiles | `.pak` files into `ConanSandbox/Mods` + `modlist.txt` | **Yes** |

Two corrections worth surfacing to whoever scoped this:
- **ARK: Survival Ascended does not use Steam Workshop.** Mods are on CurseForge (`https://arksa.curseforge.com/`), addressed by CurseForge Project ID. The Pterodactyl ASA egg's `MOD_IDS` variable says so explicitly: *"https://www.curseforge.com/ark-survival-ascended ; ProjectID is is the MOD_ID"*. CurseForge has a real partner API for hosts — a legitimate, licensed path that Steam does not offer.
- **Rust Workshop is cosmetic skins, not server maps.** The Facepunch wiki page `https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/Hosting_a_custom_map` never mentions Workshop; maps come from `+server.levelurl [url]` pointing at any direct download. Indexing Rust Workshop items would list wallpaper and clothing skins — the item I pulled live (`3613230294`) is tagged `"Wallpaper Flooring"`.

Realistically only **Barotrauma and Conan Exiles** genuinely require you to fetch bits, and Barotrauma is the one where anonymous is confirmed broken.

## B6. What LinuxGSM does — a notable negative result

I read the source. **LinuxGSM's entire mod system avoids the Steam Workshop.** `lgsm/modules/mods_list.sh` sources every mod from direct vendor HTTPS URLs (Metamod, AMX Mod X, SourceMod). `mods_core.sh` contains **zero** references to `workshop`, `steamcmd`, or `anonymous`. The only Workshop touchpoint in the whole 733-file repo is the GMod config passing the collection id to the game:
```
# lgsm/config-default/config-lgsm/gmodserver/_default.cfg
wscollectionid=""
startparameters="-game garrysmod … +host_workshop_collection ${wscollectionid} …"
```
The most widely-deployed open-source game-server manager deliberately does not act as a Workshop mirror. Worth weighing.

**Three direct hits on your plan:**
- **Caching/indexing is not addressed.** The ToU has *no* clause permitting or forbidding bulk caching of workshop metadata. It does say you may only retrieve Steam Data *"about a Steam end user"* **"as requested by the end user"** — that clause is written about *user* data and is a poor fit for workshop item metadata, but it's the closest thing to a scraping restriction and it points away from speculative bulk pre-indexing. **Genuinely ambiguous. Do not assume a catalog is permitted.**
- **100,000 calls/day** is a hard cap. At 100 items/call on `GetPublishedFileDetails`, refreshing a large catalog is feasible; `QueryFiles` discovery paging is the expensive part.
- **"not to share it with any third party… personal to you and specific to your Application"** + §13 **"may not transfer, assign, or delegate… your Steam Web API key to any third party"** — this collides head-on with the Garry's Mod install path, which requires `-authkey <Steam Web API key>` **on the game server**. If you put *your* key on customer GMod servers, you are arguably sharing/delegating it. Requiring each customer to supply their own key is the defensible design. Treat this as a real finding, not a technicality.

Also note `GetPublishedFileDetails` and `GetCollectionDetails` are **keyless**, so arguably outside "your Steam Web API key" obligations — but §4 ("You agree not to use the Steam Web API… in any way that is unlawful, or harms Valve, developers and publishers of games via Steam") applies regardless of key. Ambiguous whether keyless calls are even inside this contract, since acceptance is tied to the key sign-up form. **Unresolved.**

## C3. Steam Workshop Legal Agreement — **it no longer exists as a separate document**

`https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/workshoplegalagreement` returns **HTTP 200** with essentially one line of body content, verbatim:

> "Click <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/">here</a> to view the latest Steam Subscriber Agreement."

Confirmed by direct curl today. **There is no standalone Workshop Legal Agreement any more** — it has been folded into SSA §6 (quoted above). Any guidance, blog post or vendor policy still citing a separate "Steam Workshop Legal Agreement" is citing a dead document.

**Does the uploader's license extend to third parties / sublicensing?** Reading §6.A strictly:
- The grant runs to **"Valve and its affiliates"**. A hosting company is neither.
- Sublicensing is referenced only obliquely — *"the rights of any sub-licensees pursuant to any sub-license granted by Valve"* — which confirms Valve **may** sublicense, but **nothing in the SSA sublicenses anything to game-server hosts.**
- §6.B routes end users' rights through being a *Subscriber*: *"any Subscriber receiving distribution of your Workshop Contribution will have the same rights… as are set out in this Agreement for any other Subscriptions"* — i.e. the §2.A personal, non-commercial license. **Your customer, as a Subscriber, has a personal non-commercial license. You, as a business redistributing the file to them, do not obviously have one.**

## C4. Is a hosting company permitted to download and install workshop items onto customer servers?

**The documents do not say. I am not going to guess.** Precisely:

**What the documents do say:**
- Valve's *technical* docs plainly contemplate game servers downloading Workshop items, including anonymously (`partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/workshop/implementation`), and Valve built a Steamworks setting specifically to enable it.
- SSA §2.E grants unlimited-machine hosting rights for **Valve** Dedicated Server Software, with no non-commercial limit.
- SSA §2.G forbids reproducing/distributing Content and Services and forbids hosting "as part of content aggregation networks, websites or services, without the prior written consent of Valve."
- SSA §1.C forbids using your Account "to enable a violation of this Agreement by others, such as through their commercial use of Steam Content and Services."
- §6.B defers to **App-Specific Terms**, which for third-party games (ARK, PZ, Conan, Barotrauma, KF2, Unturned, SE, DST) are the *publishers'* EULAs — **I did not review those, and they govern.** Several mod authors also impose their own terms; the Project Zomboid mod I pulled live carries in its own description: *"Redistribution of this mod without explicit permission from the original creator is prohibited under any circumstances."*

**Where they are silent or ambiguous — be explicit about these:**
1. **No document addresses commercial game-server hosting of third-party Steam games at all.** Not the SSA, not the API ToU, not the (defunct) Workshop agreement.
2. **No Valve document states the "account must own the game" rule** for `workshop_download_item`. It is universally reported by the community and by hosts; Valve has never confirmed it in writing, and the one GitHub issue asking (`steam-for-linux#8028`) is **open with no Valve reply**.
3. **No clause addresses caching workshop metadata** for a searchable catalog.
4. **No clause addresses a host operating one purchased Steam account to service many paying customers.** §1.C is the nearest, and it cuts against you, but it is aimed at account sharing, not at a business running infrastructure. Unresolved.
5. **Whether keyless endpoints are inside the API ToU at all** is unclear, since the contract is formed at key sign-up.
6. **I found no public statement from Valve about game-server hosting providers, ever** — no blog post, no FAQ, no forum reply, no partner doc. Searched; found nothing. The absence is itself the finding.

**My honest read of the risk gradient** (not legal advice, and you should get counsel before shipping):
- **Lowest risk:** write the Workshop ID into the server's own config and let the game server fetch it through Steam. No copy passes through you. This is what the entire industry does, and it is what SSA §6.B's "Subscriber receiving distribution" language best fits. Applies to 9 of your 11 games.
- **Higher risk:** you run steamcmd under a company-owned account, pull the bits, and place them on customer machines. You are now reproducing and distributing Content and Services commercially — squarely inside §2.G's prohibition, with no clause granting an exception.
- **Highest risk:** mirroring/caching workshop files on your own storage, or serving those public DST `file_url` CDN objects yourself. Technically trivial (I proved it in one curl), legally the worst position of the three.

## C5. What hosting companies actually do today

I checked KB articles across six-plus hosts. **The pattern is uniform and telling: essentially nobody redistributes Workshop files. They write IDs into config and let the game server fetch.**

- **Host Havoc** (`https://hosthavoc.com/billing/knowledgebase/330/How-to-add-mods-to-your-Project-Zomboid-server.html`) — writes IDs only: `WorkshopItems=514427485;513111049` / `Mods=ModA;ModB`. "This method automatically adds the mod IDs to your `servertest.ini` configuration file." No file download by the host.
- **Apex Hosting** (`https://apexminecrafthosting.com/guides/project-zomboid/how-to-add-workshop-mods-to-a-project-zomboid-server/`) — has a "Steam Workshop icon" panel where you search by name or mod ID and click Install; **it automatically adds the mod IDs to the config file.** The panel is a *metadata search + config writer*, not a file mirror. This is the closest thing to what you're describing, and note carefully what it does and doesn't do.
- **Nitrado** (`https://server.nitrado.net/en-US/guides/install-mods-on-an-ark-survival-evolved-server`) — ARK mods added as ModIDs via the web interface; *"As long as you added the mod with its ID through ARK WebInterface, it will then be automatically updated."* Nitrado ships a **CurseForge** mod browser on the dashboard — a licensed, partner-API platform — but **no Steam Workshop file browser**. That choice looks deliberate.
- **Shockbyte** (`https://shockbyte.com/help/knowledgebase/articles/how-to-add-a-steam-workshop-collection-to-your-garry-s-mod-server`) — GMod: the customer creates their own public Workshop collection; the host passes the collection ID to the server.
- **PingPerfect** — same pattern for GMod (`https://pingperfect.com/knowledgebase/124/...`) and Space Engineers (`https://pingperfect.com/index.php/knowledgebase/192/How-To-Add-Mods.html`).
- **GTXGaming** — Space Engineers, the one case where they say the quiet part out loud: *"This requires a user and password of a Steam account which owns the Space Engineers game to get mods."*
- **DatHost** (`https://help.dathost.net/article/144-cs2-custom-and-workshop-maps`) — CS2 via `host_workshop_map`; the server fetches through Steam.
- **Pterodactyl/Pelican eggs**: of **216 game eggs** I downloaded and grepped, exactly **one** (Squad) calls `workshop_download_item`. Zero of the eggs for *your* eleven games do. Every one of PZ, Barotrauma, KF2, DST, Conan, Unturned runs `+login anonymous +app_update <appid>` and nothing more.

**No host makes any public claim of Valve permission**, and **I found no Valve statement about any of them.** Everyone operates in the silence.
